reserveReview.rationale: The newly issuer-linked BDO Mexico (Castillo Miranda y Compania) Q3 2026 financial valuation covers 30 September 2026 and is signed 14 October 2026. Its complete stated reserve category is 'Reserves on bank accounts' of MXN 52,030,245.12 against MXN 51,302,437.12 of MXNB in circulation, a MXN 727,808.00 surplus. Procedures identify Ethereum, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Polygon, Base and Arc supply. The report is addressed to EM EX EN CI, S. de R.L. de C.V.; this comparison does not establish a separate legal reserve claim against Nvio Pagos El Salvador. It remains an IVSC consultancy based on management-supplied documents, expressly does not confirm reserve balances with banks, expresses no named financial-assurance opinion and restricts use to management. Its scope paragraph still says March 31, 2026, while the title, numbered procedures, table and management assertions consistently specify September 30. No reserve-bank names, institution weights, withdrawal terms or instrument tenors are given. Retain probable confidence, unknown liquidity and unknown assuranceMethod. The retained Q2 source was June 30, signed July 16, with MXN 35,333,251.88 bank-account reserves and MXN 34,828,276.31 liabilities; it does not date the new portfolio.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: BDO Mexico Q3 2026 consultancy valuation: all stated reserve assets are bank-account balances; no institution split
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: The Q3 valuation report does not name the reserve banks or disclose each institution's balance, account terms, deposit protection, direct bank confirmation or an assurance opinion. Nvio and Hey Banco remain historical custody leads, not institutions independently identified by this report. The current report supplies one complete stated asset category, not institution-level composition or a bank-confirmed portfolio.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: The whitepaper states that reserves are legally and operationally segregated from issuer and affiliate operating funds and held through a single-purpose entity. It does not establish statutory bankruptcy remoteness, current provider shares, account-level allocations, or rehypothecation treatment.
